# Resizable props

## Resizable.Group

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | The axis the panels are laid out along. `"horizontal"` puts them side by side. |
| `defaultLayout` | `ResizableLayout` | — | The layout to start from, a size per panel `id` in the unit that panel declares. Read once; later changes are ignored. It works at the first render, on the server too. |
| `layout` | `ResizableLayout` | — | The layout, when you hold it yourself. A drag or key step is reported to `onLayoutChange` and applied only when you pass the new layout back. |
| `onLayoutChange` | `(layout: ResizableLayout) => void` | — | Called with the whole layout once per change a user commits: on pointer release, and on each key step. It is not called on mount, while dragging, or when the window resizes. |

## Resizable.Panel

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | required | Names the panel in a layout, so keep it stable and unique within its group. It is the layout key only: the DOM `id` is generated, so two groups on a page can reuse a name. The panel carries it as `data-panel-id`. |
| `defaultSize` | `` number \| `${number}%` \| `${number}px` `` | — | The starting size. A number is px; `"30%"` and `"240px"` carry their unit. The unit also decides what this panel's value in a layout means. A % panel without one shares what the others leave. |
| `minSize` | `` number \| `${number}%` \| `${number}px` `` | — | The least the panel can be. Same forms as `defaultSize`; a % is of the group. |
| `maxSize` | `` number \| `${number}%` \| `${number}px` `` | — | The most the panel can be. Same forms as `defaultSize`; a % is of the group. |

## Resizable.Handle

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Stops this handle from resizing. It drops out of the tab order and shows the not-allowed cursor. |
